name: help
description: List the commands (optionally only those whose name starts with a prefix). Example requests: "what can you do on the dashboard", "list dashboard commands".

prefix.description: Only commands starting with this, e.g. "lists".

name: state
description: What the dashboard is showing right now: view, clock, site, tracked objects, filters, loaded data. Example requests: "what is on the screen", "where are we", "current settings".

name: app_ready
description: Wait until the dashboard has started (and optionally until the full catalog has loaded).

full_catalog.description: Also wait for the full public catalog. Default false.

name: view_show
description: Switch the main tab. Example requests: "go to the catalog", "open the JPL tab", "show conjunctions", "back to the observer".

view.description: Also accepts: observer (tracker, tracking, passes, sky); catalog (3d, 3-d, globe, earth); ephemeris (jpl, horizons, eph, deep space); conjunctions (conjunction, close approach, close approaches, socrates).

name: time_get
description: The dashboard clock: simulated time, speed, and offset from real time. Example requests: "what time is it on the dashboard".

name: time_live
description: Return to real time at normal speed. Example requests: "go live", "back to now", "reset time".

name: time_pause
description: Freeze the clock. Example requests: "pause", "stop the animation", "freeze".

name: time_play
description: Run the clock (resume after a pause), optionally at a new speed. Example requests: "play", "play the animation", "resume", "animate".

rate.description: Simulated seconds per real second (1 = real time, 60, 1000…). Range -10000000 to 10000000.

name: time_rate
description: Set clock speed in simulated seconds per real second. 0 pauses; negative runs backward. Example requests: "speed up", "fast forward", "60 times speed", "slow down", "run backward".

name: time_set
description: Jump the clock to a date and time. ISO 8601; without an offset it is read as UTC, or as site local time with local=true. Example requests: "set the time to 9 pm", "jump to tomorrow at 6", "go to 2026-12-01 03:00 UTC".

local.description: Read a time without offset as site local time. Default false.

name: time_shift
description: Move the clock forward (positive) or back (negative). Example requests: "go forward two hours", "back 30 minutes", "skip ahead a day".

name: site_get
description: The observer site (latitude, longitude, altitude, time zone). Example requests: "where is my site", "what site are we using".

name: site_set
description: Move the observer site. Every pass, list and ephemeris is recomputed for it. Example requests: "set my site to", "observe from", "change location to".

lon.description: Degrees east (west is negative). Range -180 to 360.

alt_m.description: Metres above sea level (kept if omitted). Range -500 to 9000.

name: site_preset
description: Use one of the built-in observatory sites. Example requests: "observe from Mauna Kea", "use the Penn State site".

name.description: Also accepts: penn state (state college, psu, home, university park); paranal (cerro paranal, vlt, chile); greenwich (royal greenwich, london); mauna kea (hawaii, maunakea).

name: site_locate
description: Set the site from this computer's location (the browser may ask for permission). Example requests: "use my location", "locate me", "where am I".

name: observer_groups
description: The TLE groups the observer sidebar can load.

name: observer_group
description: Load a TLE group into the observer sidebar (Space Stations, Starlink, GPS …). Example requests: "load starlink", "show the weather satellites", "list GPS satellites".

group.description: Group id or label, e.g. "starlink", "gps-ops", "Space Stations". See observer.groups.

name: objects_find
description: Search Earth-orbiting objects by name or NORAD number across the loaded group, the full catalog and CelesTrak. Example requests: "find Hubble", "is there a satellite called", "search for Starlink 1000".

name: objects_track
description: Track an object in the observer tab (orbit, ground track, sky plot, passes). Up to 5 at once; the newest becomes primary. Example requests: "track the ISS", "show me Hubble", "follow NORAD 25544", "plot Tiangong".

object.description: Object name (e.g. "ISS", "Hubble") or NORAD catalog number (e.g. 25544).

replace.description: Stop tracking everything else first. Default false.

name: objects_untrack
description: Stop tracking one object, or all of them. Example requests: "stop tracking", "remove the ISS", "clear tracked objects".

name: objects_primary
description: Make a tracked object the primary one (data panel, sky plot focus).

object.description: Object name (e.g. "ISS", "Hubble") or NORAD catalog number (e.g. 25544).

name: objects_tracked
description: The tracked objects with where they are now, the current or next pass, and the next naked-eye pass. Example requests: "when does it rise", "is the ISS up", "what am I tracking".

name: objects_info
description: Everything about one Earth-orbiting object without changing the screen: orbital elements, position and pointing now (J2000 RA/Dec), and its passes over the site. Example requests: "tell me about Hubble", "is the ISS visible tonight", "when is the next Tiangong pass", "where is NORAD 20580".

object.description: Object name (e.g. "ISS", "Hubble") or NORAD catalog number (e.g. 25544).

hours.description: How far ahead to list passes. Range 1 to 72. Default 24.

name: objects_download_tle
description: Download the primary tracked object's element set as a .txt file.

name: observer_horizon
description: Forecast horizon for tracked objects (how far ahead orbits and passes are drawn). Example requests: "show the next 6 hours", "forecast 24 hours".

name: observer_plot
description: Right-hand plot: sky plot (alt/az dome) or ground track (map). Example requests: "show the sky plot", "switch to the map", "show ground track".

plot.description: Also accepts: sky (skyplot, sky plot, dome, polar); groundtrack (ground track, map, gt, track).

name: observer_frame
description: 3-D orbit view frame: inertial (ECI) or Earth-fixed (ECEF). Example requests: "show inertial frame", "switch to earth fixed".

frame.description: Also accepts: inertial (eci, teme, j2000, space fixed); earthfixed (ecef, earth fixed, rotating, itrf).

name: skyplot_options
description: Sky plot options: draw every pass in the horizon (not just the next) and/or only naked-eye-visible segments. Example requests: "show all passes on the sky plot", "only visible passes".

name: observer_conditions
description: Observing weather at the site for the coming hours (cloud cover, wind, rain chance, temperature); can open or refresh the panel. Example requests: "is it cloudy tonight", "what is the weather for observing", "show observing conditions".

open.description: Open (true) or close (false) the conditions panel.

name: observer_export_csv
description: Download the primary object's pass table as CSV.

name: lists_show
description: Show one of the site lists under the observer tab, optionally setting filters. Passes, in-view and GEO lists cover the whole public catalog. Example requests: "show debris overhead", "what is above me", "show upcoming passes", "show geostationary satellites I can see".

tab.description: Also accepts: tracked (selected, my objects, tracked objects); passes (upcoming, current and upcoming, next passes, rising); inview (in view, overhead, above, up now); geo (always in view, geostationary, geosynchronous, geo belt).

type.description: Object type to show. Also accepts: all (everything, all objects, any); payload (payloads, satellite, satellites, active); rb (rocket body, rocket bodies, r/b, rockets); debris (junk, fragments, deb).

name.description: Only names or NORAD numbers containing this text ("" clears).

hours.description: Passes list: how many hours ahead.

min_elevation.description: Passes list: only passes whose peak is above this many degrees.

visible_only.description: Passes list: only naked-eye-visible passes (sunlit object, dark sky).

exclude_daytime.description: Passes list: hide passes that peak in daylight.

name: lists_filter
description: Change filters on the site lists without switching list. Example requests: "only debris", "only visible ones", "payloads only", "clear the filter", "next 6 hours".

type.description: Object type to show. Also accepts: all (everything, all objects, any); payload (payloads, satellite, satellites, active); rb (rocket body, rocket bodies, r/b, rockets); debris (junk, fragments, deb).

name.description: Only names or NORAD numbers containing this text ("" clears).

hours.description: Passes list: how many hours ahead.

min_elevation.description: Passes list: only passes whose peak is above this many degrees.

visible_only.description: Passes list: only naked-eye-visible passes (sunlit object, dark sky).

exclude_daytime.description: Passes list: hide passes that peak in daylight.

name: lists_get
description: Read a site list as data (shows it on screen too). Waits for the catalog and the pass scan to finish. Example requests: "how many objects are overhead", "which debris is above me", "what passes are coming up", "list the visible passes".

tab.description: Defaults to the list on screen. Also accepts: tracked (selected, my objects, tracked objects); passes (upcoming, current and upcoming, next passes, rising); inview (in view, overhead, above, up now); geo (always in view, geostationary, geosynchronous, geo belt).

type.description: Object type to show. Also accepts: all (everything, all objects, any); payload (payloads, satellite, satellites, active); rb (rocket body, rocket bodies, r/b, rockets); debris (junk, fragments, deb).

name.description: Only names or NORAD numbers containing this text ("" clears).

hours.description: Passes list: how many hours ahead.

min_elevation.description: Passes list: only passes whose peak is above this many degrees.

visible_only.description: Passes list: only naked-eye-visible passes (sunlit object, dark sky).

exclude_daytime.description: Passes list: hide passes that peak in daylight.

name: lists_recalculate
description: Recompute the passes list from the current clock.

name: catalog_filter
description: Show all objects, payloads, debris or rocket bodies in the 3-D catalog. Example requests: "show only debris in the catalog", "show rocket bodies", "show everything".

type.description: Object type to show. Also accepts: all (everything, all objects, any); payload (payloads, satellite, satellites, active); rb (rocket body, rocket bodies, r/b, rockets); debris (junk, fragments, deb).

name: catalog_buckets
description: Choose which data sets the 3-D catalog loads (full catalog, Starlink, GPS, debris clouds …) and reload. Example requests: "add starlink to the catalog", "load only the GEO belt".

name: catalog_counts
description: How many objects the 3-D catalog holds, by class. Example requests: "how many objects are in orbit", "how much debris is there".

name: catalog_select
description: Highlight one object in the 3-D catalog, draw its orbit and open its card. Example requests: "show me where the ISS is in the catalog", "highlight Hubble".

object.description: Object name (e.g. "ISS", "Hubble") or NORAD catalog number (e.g. 25544).

name: catalog_deselect
description: Clear the highlighted object in the 3-D catalog.

name: catalog_track_selected
description: Send the highlighted catalog object to the observer tab for tracking.

name: camera_zoom
description: Zoom the 3-D view in or out. Example requests: "zoom out", "zoom in", "closer", "further away".

direction.description: Also accepts: in (closer, nearer); out (further, farther, away, back).

view.description: Which 3-D view (defaults to the one on screen). Default "current".

name: camera_rotate
description: Turn the 3-D view. Example requests: "rotate left", "look from above", "tilt down".

view.description: Which 3-D view (defaults to the one on screen). Default "current".

name: camera_reset
description: Put the 3-D view back to its starting angle and distance. Example requests: "reset the view", "recenter".

view.description: Which 3-D view (defaults to the one on screen). Default "current".

name: eph_resolve
description: Find a deep-space object in JPL Horizons by name or number without plotting it. Example requests: "look up Maruthiakella", "what is the Horizons id of CAPSTONE".

name: eph_plot
description: Plot a planet, moon, asteroid, comet or spacecraft from JPL Horizons and return its visibility from the site. Example requests: "plot Mars", "show CAPSTONE", "add Kathleenhowell", "plot Artemis II".

name: eph_visibility
description: Is a deep-space object visible from the site now, and when in the next 72 hours (elevation limit, astronomical darkness). Example requests: "is Maruthiakella visible from my site", "can I see Jupiter tonight", "when is Mars up", "is CAPSTONE still tracked".

target.description: Defaults to the active ephemeris target.

name: eph_focus
description: Make one of the plotted targets the active one.

name: eph_remove
description: Remove a plotted target, or all of them.

name: eph_list
description: Plotted targets and the built-in target list.

name: eph_min_elevation
description: Elevation limit (degrees) used for ephemeris visibility windows.

name: eph_refetch
description: Fetch the active target again from JPL Horizons.

name: solar_scale
description: Solar-system map scale: compact (readable) or true linear distances.

mode.description: Also accepts: compact (compressed, log, readable); true (true scale, linear, real, actual).

name: solar_rate
description: Animate the solar-system map at this many days per second. Example requests: "speed up the planets", "run the solar system".

name: solar_step
description: Step the clock by a number of days (for the solar-system map; affects every view).

name: conj_list
description: Predicted close approaches between catalogued objects (CelesTrak SOCRATES). Example requests: "any close approaches", "what conjunctions are coming", "riskiest conjunctions".

sort.description: Order (defaults to the one on screen). Also accepts: range (distance, miss distance, closest); tca (time, soonest, next); probability (prob, pc, risk, likelihood).

name: conj_select
description: Open one conjunction (by rank in the current order, or by an object in it) and draw the encounter.

object.description: Name or NORAD number of either object.

name: conj_refresh
description: Fetch the SOCRATES report again.

name: spaceweather_get
description: Planetary K index and 10.7 cm solar flux from NOAA SWPC (drag and aurora conditions). Example requests: "how is space weather", "is there a geomagnetic storm", "what is Kp".

name: share_link
description: A web address that opens the dashboard in its current state (view, site, tracked objects, list, filters, target). Example requests: "give me a link to this view", "share this".

name: ui_caption
description: Show a short caption at the bottom of the dashboard (for example what Claire is saying). Empty text hides it.

seconds.description: 0 keeps it until replaced. Range 0 to 120. Default 6.
